safety check\/call prior to cockpit entr: Safety Check Prior to Cockpit Entry
Safety Check Prior to Leaving the Aircraft

overview: This event is your introduction to operating in the T-6B cockpit. You will practice checklist discipline, challenge-action-response procedures, crew coordination, ground handling signals, and safety checks before entering and leaving the aircraft. You will also begin building cockpit familiarity through blind cockpit checks and repeated strap-in practice.

studyNotes.headline: Discussion items

items.text: All checklists are run using challenge-action-response.
State the checklist item first.
Perform the required action.
State the correct response or position.
For switches or controls that require a check, physically touch or visually verify the item.
If the switch or control is not in the correct position, move it to the proper setting before responding.
Checklist flow should always be smooth, deliberate, and standardized.
Example flow:
Both pilots are responsible for ensuring every checklist item is completed correctly.
The IP has overall responsibility, but the student is still expected to catch mistakes or missed items.
Some checklist items require responses from both cockpits.
When dual concurrence is required, do not continue until the other crewmember has responded.
Good CRM means staying engaged, listening carefully, and speaking up if something is skipped or incorrect.
Checklist discipline is a shared responsibility.
Most checklists are not memorized and should be run with the quadfold or checklist guide.

Even after memorizing these checklists, the quadfold should still remain available as backup.
